pr_title: improve error handling & map stack trace
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/498

- Improves the output of localStorage (gets rid of double escapes).
- Tries to map error stack trace using source maps (using https://github.com/stacktracejs/stacktrace.js). ~~No clue if this is going to work in production -- depends whether we deploy source maps. We'll see.~~ looks like it does on preview:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/75096103-7ab28380-559c-11ea-9386-365fede077d1.png)

Repro:

1. load https://excalidraw-git-improveerrorhandling.vjeux.now.sh//?id=5142238724096000
2. click on the text element
pr_comments:
This pull request is being automatically deployed with ZEIT Now ([learn more](https://zeit.ink/github-learn-more)).
To see the status of your deployment, click below or on the icon next to each commit.

  🔍 Inspect: https://zeit.co/vjeux/excalidraw/255t70l69
  ✅ Preview: https://excalidraw-git-improveerrorhandling.vjeux.now.sh
Btw, I've noticed that multiple errors tend to bubble to the error boundary, but we only log (display in the textarea) the stack trace of the last error. Should I display all of them?

I've moved from `getDerivedStateFromError` to `componentDidCatch` because it seems that returning state from `getDerivedStateFromError` multiple times does not update state.

WTBS, the [docs mention](https://reactjs.org/docs/react-component.html#componentdidcatch):

> In the event of an error, you can render a fallback UI with componentDidCatch() by calling setState, but this will be deprecated in a future release. Use static getDerivedStateFromError() to handle fallback rendering instead.

which is sad, but let's burn that bridge when we come to it (unless someone has a better idea).
Merging as it's best to get this to production sooner rather than later.

issue_context.title: Map error stack traces to source
issue_context.body:
The error stack traces retrieved from `error.stack` (in recent #493) isn't mapped to source (if user instead opens devTools, Chrome *does* map it to source).

To reproduce this, you can load <https://excalidraw.com/?id=5142238724096000> and click on the rendered text element to trigger the error.

We can use a library such as [stacktrace.js](https://github.com/stacktracejs/stacktrace.js) to get mapped stack traces.
